claims.text: A thin Ni interlayer on a Cu substrate will improve adhesion of an overlying high-entropy-alloy coating relative to direct deposition.
A thin Ni interlayer will improve the wear performance of an overlying high-entropy-alloy coating on Cu.
Ni bonds well with the unspecified high-entropy alloy.
Ni has an intermediate thermal expansion behavior relative to Cu and the high-entropy-alloy coating.
Ni has intermediate chemical properties relative to Cu and the high-entropy-alloy coating.
The thermal-expansion and chemical properties of Ni promote robust metallurgical bonding between Cu and the high-entropy alloy.
A Ni interlayer reduces poor adhesion associated with direct high-entropy-alloy deposition on Cu.
A Ni interlayer reduces problematic interdiffusion associated with direct high-entropy-alloy deposition on Cu.
Direct deposition of a high-entropy alloy on Cu is prone to weak adhesion.
Direct deposition of a high-entropy alloy on Cu is prone to interdiffusion problems.
Avoiding deleterious intermetallic-phase formation is necessary for the expected adhesion and performance improvement.
Avoiding significant high-temperature diffusion is necessary for the expected adhesion and performance improvement.
Stronger interfacial bonding produced by the Ni interlayer will enhance surface protection of the Cu matrix.
